transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me?

Yeah, thanks. Um, I guess I came in because people have been pointing out how I'm acting... well, how I'm moving, really. Like they can actually see me moving like I’m underwater. Taking forever just to answer someone or even just to get out of a chair. I have this one chair, actually, this awful brown corduroy recliner I found on the curb back when I was taking a few classes at the community college. Man, that was a weird time. I took this astronomy class thinking it'd just be looking at constellations, but the math was completely ridiculous. The professor always wore these crazy bright bow ties and brought his own chalk to class... anyway, where was I? 

Oh, right. So I either get stuck moving super slow, or it's the total opposite. I'll just be pacing my apartment for hours, rubbing my hands together like I’m trying to shake off a bad call. I do customer service for a living, so I get a lot of bad calls. You wouldn't believe how nasty people get over shipping fees. Just Tuesday this guy screamed at me for ten minutes straight because his package was a day late, like I personally drove the delivery truck and hid it from him. People just forget there's a human being on the other end of the phone, you know? But yeah... the pacing and the slow moving, that's why my family wanted me to come in.

Over these same weeks when you've been moving very slowly or pacing, have you noticed a significant change in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or on the other end, unusually elated, irritable, or 'wired'?

Wired? I mean, I don't know about wired, unless you count all the coffee I drink. I actually just bought this French press last week because my buddy Dave swore it would change my life. Dave’s the guy who helped me move that awful corduroy chair into my place, actually. He drives this absolute junker of a Honda Civic, right? The thing always smells like pine needles and old gym socks, and the muffler is so loud you can hear him coming from three blocks away. We had to tie the chair to the roof with these cheap bungee cords... it was a whole ordeal. We almost lost it on the highway. 

But, uh, what were you asking? Oh, right, my mood. Um, no, I haven't really noticed feeling super sad or hopeless or anything like that. Just... normal, I guess? I don't feel unusually happy or irritable either, really. Just me. I just get stuck or I pace. So yeah, no big mood changes that I can think of. Mostly I'm just trying to figure out how to clean the wet coffee grounds out of the bottom of that French press, honestly. It's a total pain. Have you ever used one of those?
Have you experienced anything like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or had thoughts or beliefs that others have told you seem unusual or not based in reality?

Um, voices? I mean... I don't know if this counts, but sometimes I hear the beep from my work headset. Like, that little electronic chime that means a call is coming in. Or I'll hear this voice, kinda sounds like my old supervisor, Brenda. She'll just say my name, or she'll say "too slow." But the weird thing is, I'll hear it when my laptop is completely closed and I'm not even working. 

Brenda was something else, let me tell you. She used to walk around the call center floor with this giant Yeti cup—one of those bright pink ones—and she was always chewing ice. Just *crunch, crunch, crunch* right in your ear while you're trying to de-escalate a customer. She had this weird rule where we couldn't have any personal items on our desks, not even a picture of a dog. I had this little plastic dinosaur, a Stegosaurus, that I got from a cereal box when I was a kid. I kept it next to my monitor for years, and she made me throw it away. Said it was "unprofessional." Like the customer on the phone can see my plastic dinosaur, right? It was ridiculous. I actually saw her at the grocery store a few months ago, in the produce aisle, squeezing all the avocados. I almost went up and said something, but... I don't know. 

Anyway, yeah, I hear the headset beep or Brenda telling me I'm too slow, even when there's no phone ringing. So... is that what you mean by unusual?
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, neurological problems, new medications, or changes in substance or alcohol use around the time these movement and speech changes started?

Um, no, nothing like that. I haven't been sick or anything, and I don't really take any medications. Well, except ibuprofen sometimes for my back. Sitting in that computer chair all day really does a number on my lower back. I tried getting one of those lumbar support pillows, the ones that strap to the back of the chair? But the strap broke after like a week. It was just this cheap elastic. I got it off Amazon, and the reviews were all five stars, but I'm pretty sure they were fake. Have you noticed how many fake reviews there are now? It's like you can't trust anything you buy online anymore. I was reading this article about how there are whole companies whose only job is to write fake reviews for products. They just sit in these big rooms and type out lies all day. Kind of makes you wonder about the people doing that job, right? Like, do they go home and feel good about what they did that day? 

But yeah, no new meds or illnesses or anything. And I don't really drink much, maybe a beer if I'm watching a game, but that's it. So... no, nothing like that going on.
Along with the slow movements and pacing, have you noticed any physical symptoms like fever, excessive sweating, a racing heart, or unusual muscle stiffness?

Um, no, no fever or anything like that. My heart hasn't been racing, and I haven't been sweating more than usual. I mean, it's pretty hot in my apartment right now because the AC unit in the window is acting up. It makes this horrible rattling sound, like there's a bunch of loose screws just bouncing around inside the fan blades. I tried calling the landlord about it, but you know how that goes. He's this guy named Gary who always wears these really bright, tropical shirts, even in the middle of winter. He told me he'd send someone out "next week," but he said that three weeks ago. I even tried taking the front panel off myself to see if I could figure out what was rattling, but it's held on by these weird star-shaped screws. Who even has a screwdriver for those? I had to go down to the hardware store on 4th street—the one with the really creaky wooden floors—just to look for a special bit. But the guy working there was totally unhelpful, just stood there texting on his phone the whole time. 

So yeah, no sweating or fever or stiff muscles or anything. Just dealing with the broken AC and trying not to melt in my living room. Have you ever tried to fix a window unit yourself?
How long have you been experiencing these episodes of slow movement, pacing, and hearing Brenda's voice or the headset beep—has this been going on for weeks, months, or longer?

Um, let's see... it's been a while now. I'd say about two years and three months? Yeah, it started right after I got fired from that customer support job. Which, by the way, was completely unfair. They said my "handle time" was too high, but I was just trying to actually help the customers instead of rushing them off the phone like everyone else did. 

There was this one lady, Mrs. Higgins, she called in because she couldn't figure out how to reset her password. She was like eighty years old and lived alone in this huge house in Maine. We ended up talking for like forty-five minutes about her garden. She grew these massive heirloom tomatoes, the big ugly ones that taste amazing? She said the trick is to put crushed eggshells in the soil before you plant them. I actually tried it last spring. I bought this little self-watering planter for my windowsill—because, you know, no yard—and I saved up all my eggshells from breakfast for a month. I felt kind of weird just having a bowl of eggshells sitting on my counter, honestly. My buddy Dave came over and asked if I was starting a compost pile in my kitchen. Dave's always making jokes like that. He just bought this old beat-up RV and thinks he's going to renovate it and travel the country, but he doesn't even know how to change a tire. 

But yeah, anyway, the pacing and the slow moving and hearing Brenda and the beeps... that's been going on for about two years and three months, ever since they let me go from that job.
Have you or others noticed times when you stay completely still in one position for a long while, resist being moved, or stop talking altogether?

Um, completely still? I don't know about completely stopping talking, but... well, when I get overwhelmed, I sometimes catch myself just standing in the kitchen. Like, I'll have my coffee mug halfway to my mouth and I just freeze there. Or I'll find myself walking the same little loop by the couch for no real reason. 

Speaking of coffee, I actually had to switch to decaf recently because regular was making me too jittery. But decaf tastes so different, doesn't it? It's like it's missing that... that bite. I tried buying this fancy organic Swiss water process kind from the grocery store. The bag had this really nice drawing of a mountain on it, like the Alps or something. Have you ever been to Switzerland? I always thought it would be cool to go there and ride one of those scenic trains through the mountains. I saw a documentary about them on PBS late one night. The trains have these huge glass roofs so you can see the peaks while you sit there eating fondue. I love cheese, but fondue seems like a really messy thing to eat on a moving train. What if the train hits a bump and you spill boiling cheese all over yourself? That sounds like a nightmare. I guess they must have really smooth tracks over there. 

But yeah, I do get stuck sometimes. Just standing there with my mug, or doing that little loop by the couch.

She said the trick is to put crushed eggshells in the soil before you plant them. I actually tried it last spring. I bought this little self-watering planter for my windowsill—because, you know, no yard—and I saved up all my eggshells from breakfast for a month. I felt kind of weird just having a bowl of eggshells sitting on my counter, honestly. My buddy Dave came over and asked if I was starting a compost pile in my kitchen. Dave's always making jokes like that. He just bought this old beat-up RV and thinks he's going to renovate it and travel the country, but he doesn't even know how to change a tire. 

But yeah, anyway, the pacing and the slow moving and hearing Brenda and the beeps... that's been going on for about two years and three months, ever since they let me go from that job.

inference.note: No fever, tachycardia, diaphoresis, muscle rigidity, illness, medication, or substance use identified, making an organic/medical cause (F06.1) less likely. Chronic (2+ years) psychosis with persistent auditory hallucinations and catatonic-like motor symptoms (slowed movement, pacing) without any mood episode supports primary psychotic disorder, consistent with catatonic schizophrenia.

doctor.intent: Assess for specific catatonic motor signs (e.g., remaining fixed in one position for long periods, resisting movement, or not speaking at all) to confirm catatonia-type features supporting the diagnosis.
doctor.question: Have you or others noticed times when you stay completely still in one position for a long while, resist being moved, or stop talking altogether?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: When I get overwhelmed, I sometimes catch myself standing in the kitchen with my coffee mug halfway to my mouth or walking the same little loop by the couch for no real reason.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about catatonic behaviors such as staying completely still in one position, which matches the manifestation of standing with a coffee mug halfway to the mouth.

patient.answer:
Um, completely still? I don't know about completely stopping talking, but... well, when I get overwhelmed, I sometimes catch myself just standing in the kitchen. Like, I'll have my coffee mug halfway to my mouth and I just freeze there. Or I'll find myself walking the same little loop by the couch for no real reason. 

Speaking of coffee, I actually had to switch to decaf recently because regular was making me too jittery. But decaf tastes so different, doesn't it? It's like it's missing that... that bite. I tried buying this fancy organic Swiss water process kind from the grocery store. The bag had this really nice drawing of a mountain on it, like the Alps or something. Have you ever been to Switzerland? I always thought it would be cool to go there and ride one of those scenic trains through the mountains. I saw a documentary about them on PBS late one night. The trains have these huge glass roofs so you can see the peaks while you sit there eating fondue. I love cheese, but fondue seems like a really messy thing to eat on a moving train. What if the train hits a bump and you spill boiling cheese all over yourself? That sounds like a nightmare. I guess they must have really smooth tracks over there. 

But yeah, I do get stuck sometimes. Just standing there with my mug, or doing that little loop by the couch.

inference.note: Chronic (2+ years) catatonic symptoms (psychomotor retardation, freezing/waxy immobility, pacing) with persistent auditory hallucinations, no mood episode, no substance/medical cause identified—consistent with schizophrenia, catatonic type. No new findings altered the differential.
